data: Skeleton entry for /fleet (PRD-012 v0.2 / Phase A scaffold). Builder + agency + first-flight per public sources. Specs and gallery TBD in later phases.

Skylab was America's first space station, and one of history's great acts of improvisation — an entire orbital workshop built inside the empty hydrogen tank of a spent Saturn V upper stage. Rather than design a station from scratch, NASA converted the hardware the cancelled Moon landings had left over into a house-sized laboratory with crew quarters, a shower, and a crewed solar observatory. Nearly destroyed at launch when its sun shield tore away, it was saved by the first crew's improvised repairs and went on to prove the thing every later station assumed: that people can live and work in orbit for months, and fix their spacecraft when it breaks.

America’s first space station, built from a Saturn V S-IVB upper stage. Three crews of three each lived aboard between 1973 and 1974, conducting solar observations and zero-g experiments. Reentered uncontrolled over Australia in 1979.
First crewed Skylab visit — repaired the damaged workshop and saved the programme
Second Skylab crew — 59 days, deployed twin-pole solar shield to replace parasol
Longest Skylab stay — 84 days, observed Comet Kohoutek, disputed "Skylab strike" rest day
Lifted Apollo 7, Skylab crews, and ASTP
Apollo 10 + Skylab + 53 Shuttle flights; now NASA's SLS / Artemis pad
First Almaz military station — depressurised on orbit before any crew arrived; reentered 1973-05-28 after 54 days
Second Almaz military station — Soyuz 14 crew Jul 1974; Soyuz 15 failed automatic docking; reportedly tested an onboard cannon 1975-01-24
Civilian DOS-4 station — hosted Soyuz 17 (29 days) + Soyuz 18 (63 days, then-longest spaceflight) crews; deorbited 1977-02-03
Last Almaz military station — Soyuz 21 + Soyuz 24 crews; Soyuz 23 failed approach; reentered 1977-08-08 after 412 days
Pieces of Skylab that fell around Esperance when the station re-entered on 11 July 1979
The backup Skylab orbital workshop, which you can walk through
